title: Oertel's conjecture on the mixed-integer volume
statement:
Let $C\subset\mathbb{R}^{n+d}$ be a convex body and let $S=C\cap(\mathbb{Z}^n\times\mathbb{R}^d)$. For a mixed-integer set $S$, write

$$
\mathcal{F}(S)=\max_{\mathbf{x}\in S}\left(\inf\\{\mu(H\cap S):H\text{ is a halfspace with }\mathbf{x}\in H\\}\right)
$$

for its Oertel radius. **Oertel's conjecture.** The Oertel radius satisfies

$$
\mathcal{F}(S)\geq\frac{1}{2^n}\frac{1}{e}.
$$

This conjecture proposes a universal lower bound for the mixed-integer volume of halfspaces through a centerpoint, extending the role of Grünbaum-type inequalities to mixed-integer convex optimization. The supplied source does not indicate whether the conjecture has been resolved.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.11864

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).
source_name: Andrés Cristi and David Salas, “Reducing the Large Set Threshold for Oertel's Conjecture on the Mixed-Integer Volume”, arXiv:2411.11864 (2026).
